after: This demand covers Infrastructure Services activities required to support the global Real Estate portfolio, including new site openings, office relocations, site consolidations, expansions, and site closures. Scope includes campus networking (Cisco/Juniper LAN), WAN connectivity, NAC, micro-segmentation, wireless infrastructure, collaboration and meeting room technologies, AV/display equipment, equipment room setup, and associated implementation services. Infrastructure requirements are directly driven by Real Estate projects and must be delivered before site occupancy, business transition, or site closure can be completed. The €2.5M request represents estimated 2027 project investments required to support the currently identified Real Estate portfolio across regions and is based on historical deployment patterns, expected site volumes, infrastructure refresh requirements, and infrastructure components required for new and relocated facilities. Cost estimates are intentionally high-level because detailed site designs become available only after Real Estate projects are formally approved. This demand is categorized under Decommissioning/Replatforming, due to a significant portion of the investment enables retirement and removal of infrastructure assets associated with site closures and consolidations, avoidance of parallel infrastructure operations during relocations, and migration to modern network architectures incorporating NAC, micro-segmentation, and WAN modernization Cost of not doing: Real Estate programs would be unable to execute site openings, closures, and relocations on time; regulatory, security, and operational requirements would not be met; and Philips would face project delays, business disruption, increased risk from legacy infrastructure, and potential duplicate operating costs during site transitions

before: eliminates recurring $96K upgrade costs and delivers $50K cloud savings per year across 14 sites
after: Elimination of recurring Cache upgrade costs (~$96K). Cloud infrastructure savings of approximately $50K per site. Reduced operational effort associated with distributed file-share management. Simplification of the storage landscape across 14 locations. Reduced technical debt and improved maintainability of the file-sharing platform. The decommissioning component is the retirement of the existing Cache-based file-sharing platform following successful migration to the new architecture. Savings realization is contingent upon full migration completion and retirement of legacy infrastructure components supporting the current platform.

name: Cloud File Share Solution (CFSS)
before: Cache loss results in factories having to call off shifts
after: Cache loss results in factories having to call off shifts. Philips continues to incur recurring upgrade costs, remains constrained by current platform limitations, increases future migration complexity, and delays consolidation of file-sharing services onto a modern cloud-ready architecture.

name: Cloud File Share Solution (CFSS)
before: Global
after: CFSS is a replatforming initiative intended to replace the current Cache-based file-sharing solution used across 14 sites with a modern cloud-enabled file sharing architecture based on Nutanix Unified Storage (NUS) and PeerGFS technologies. The current platform has functional limitations and requires recurring upgrade activities that generate approximately $96K of upgrade-related costs during each major refresh cycle. The proposed solution addresses scalability, synchronization, file-locking, resiliency, and operational constraints of the current environment while simplifying the storage landscape and providing a more sustainable long-term architecture. Scope includes solution design, platform deployment, migration activities, validation, performance testing, and rollout preparation across participating sites.

before: Consolidation of Business partners by moving customers master data and vendor master data as well to IDMC (MDM SaaS). The reason for this investment: on 27 July 2026 the external platform released the Q2 2026 results early, during US trading hours. This forced an unplanned market disclosure by the Board of Management and Disclosure Committee, formal AFM and SEC (6-K) filings and a 30-minute trading halt. This investment removes the cause: results are released only by Philips, on the Philips platform, through a controlled manual step.
Financial value at risk:
– Share price: each 1% fall is about €214M of shareholder value (Philips market value about €21.4B, 25 Sep 2026). Precedent: ASML fell 16% (more than $52B) on the day its results appeared early on its own website (Oct 2024).
– Fines: the AFM fined SBM Offshore €2M for late disclosure of inside information (2019); the EU MAR maximum is 2% of turnover or more (about €360M).
Break-even: the €400K requested equals about 0.002% of Philips' market value – under 0.2% of what a 1% share-price fall would cost.

Hard benefit: €178K per year once the external Results Hub platform is retired (€118K platform and licence fees, about €60K operational and maintenance support); payback about 2.2 years.
Other benefits (Disclosure Committee paper): one simple corporate publication channel, direct Philips ownership and control, fewer parties with clearer ownership, results aligned with the Investor Relations and Communications pages.

name: 3PL Transformation (Dual 3PL ) - India
after: The project improves the reliability, visibility and control of PH logistics operations in India by enabling a dual-3PL model with stronger system integration and governance. It supports more timely and accurate deliveries, better management of customer claims and audits through real-time shipment tracking and digital proof of delivery, and reduces manual work in logistics documentation. It also strengthens operational decision-making by providing earlier visibility of delivery and service-performance issues.

name: 3PL Transformation (Dual 3PL ) - India
before: Strategic distribution capability
after: If this project is not implemented, PH India will remain dependent on the current 3PL set-up, with continued risk of delayed and incorrect deliveries, high returns, quality issues and customer claims. Limited system integration and weak adoption of logistics technology will also restrict shipment visibility, traceability and governance, increasing indirect costs such as freight and lost business while making it harder to achieve the required Fill Rate and delivery-performance targets.

name: RegMem in a Day
after: RegMem in a Day enables PH to implement regulatory packaging changes much faster and at scale across businesses and markets. It reduces the volume of artwork changes requiring full management, lowers excess-stock and repacking risk, and shortens regulatory-change throughput time from up to 12 months to around three weeks. The solution also helps ensure products reach customers without regulatory roadblocks and supports serial-number and anti-counterfeit marking integration.
